title: Exascale Storage I/O: Managing Data Movement at Scale
problem: Exascale simulations generate massive I/O workloads and require efficient data movement across multiple memory hierarchy levels to avoid becoming bottlenecked.
motivation: I/O and data movement are critical performance and energy bottlenecks in exascale computing that constrain scientific simulation throughput.
method: Proposes a hierarchical storage management system that analyzes runtime I/O patterns and optimizes data placement and movement decisions across memory levels (registers, cache, DRAM, burst buffers, persistent storage).
key_novelty: Adaptive hierarchical storage management that dynamically optimizes data movement based on observed I/O access patterns in exascale applications.
contributions: Characterization of I/O patterns in exascale simulations
Data movement optimization across memory hierarchy
limitations: Limited discussion of scalability; applicability beyond simulation workloads unclear
primary_theme: Optimizing data movement in exascale storage systems
